# Magnitude: The Local Open Source Definitive AI Engine (Rode LLMs on your PC!)

Magnitude is a local and open source inference engine to run AI models on the computer you already have. The video shows how it analyzes the hardware and chooses the model, loads the models on demand, protects the memory and connects to programming agents.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on September 11, 2026 (8 min 22 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8z4JuiIOT58

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## Why local AI is difficult

Many people want a 100% private and unsigned AI, but the technical effort to make it work is a barrier [00:00]. Magnitude is a local and open source inference engine that tries to remove this barrier [00:22].

Those who have already configured models at home know the cycle of trial and error: GGUF files, quantization limits that can spoil the model and locking due to lack of memory [00:43].

The AI in the cloud is powerful, but has continuous cost, risk of privacy and limits of use [01:46]. The traditional local AI is free and private, but unstable and difficult to adjust [02:08]. According to the video, the current hardware has plenty of power; one orchestrator was missing [02:08].

## End of manual configuration

Magnitude does the work in four steps [02:28]:

- Analyze the available processor and memory [02:28].
- Catalog and rank the best model combinations [02:50].
- Download and configure everything by yourself [02:50].
- Start the model already connected to the agent of your preference [02:50].

The ranking weighs the expected speed, model quality and quantization, and compares the size of the context window with the memory that really remains [03:12].

It runs on Apple Silicon, on NVIDIA and AMD cards and only on CPU, Linux and Windows by WSL [03:33].

## Loading on demand

Before, climbing a model occupied much of the memory until the process was closed [04:15]. In Magnitude, models stay on disk and only go to memory when an agent sends a command [04:15].

The video uses an analogy: the model is an encyclopedia on the shelf (the disk) that only goes to the table (the memory) at the time of reading and comes back later [04:35].

## Memory management

Memory usage changes all the time because of the browser and other programs [05:16]. Therefore, Magnitude confers real-time memory and only carries the model if there is a security margin [05:16].

- Download the models when they are inactive [05:38].
- Redo the memory calculation before each new load [05:38].
- Interrupt the inference if the memory falls too much, and preserves the state of the prompt not to lose context [05:38].

## Integration with agents

Open models usually have different reasoning formats and chat templates, which breaks the tools [06:00]. Magnitude normalizes this and presents a single interface, so the tools change models without rewriting code [06:22].

It works with Magnitude Harness and tools like Claude Code, Cline and Codex [06:43]. The engine displays local APIs in the OpenAI and Anthropic standard, so the agents talk to it as if talking to the cloud [07:03].

## Cost and privacy

The cost of each call is zero: no tuition, no package of tokens and no API key [07:23]. The code and the prompts do not leave the machine [07:23].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Magnitude run on Windows?

Yes, by WSL. It also runs on macOS with Apple Silicon and Linux [03:33].

### The model keeps occupying the memory all the time?

Nope. The models stay on the disk and only go to memory when an agent asks, and are unloaded when they are inactive [04:15].

## About the video

O **Magnitude** is a local inference engine and *open source* developed to run the best AI models directly on the hardware you already have, be it a Mac, a NVIDIA/AMD GPU or just CPU. Excuse me. Apache 2.0, it offers a 100% free, private solution without API costs or request limits.

In this video, we explain how Magnitude analyzes the processor, memory and bandwidth of your system to recommend the optimal combination of model, quantization and context size. In addition, we detail how your server in the background loads models on demand and connects natively to various agents and tools such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex, Claude Code, Oh My Pi and Cline.

🚀 **Quick Installation in Terminal:**
```bash
npm i -g @magnitudedev/cli
magnitude setup
```
*(You can also install using `bun`, `pnpm` or `yarn`).*
